card.name: Linking words before named antiviral drugs
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as 'with', 'containing', 'are' or '+' that come right before a drug name. Seen mostly in hepatitis B flare warnings for HIV/HBV drugs and in drug-combination lists.

modes.label: Discontinued products containing
modes.description: The word 'containing' or 'with' after 'discontinued products' or 'therapy', just before the drug names.
modes.example: have discontinued products<< containing>> emtricitabine and/or ten

modes.label: Treated with a drug
modes.description: The word 'with' after 'treated' or 'therapy', just before a brand or generic drug name.
modes.example: occurred in patients treated<< with>> Lynparza [see Adverse Re

modes.label: Plus sign in regimens
modes.description: A '+' or a comma inside a combination regimen, just before the next drug.

card.writes: It seems to lower the chance of words about finishing or completion after the linking word.
card.plain: It fires on the small joining word just before a drug name in warnings about stopping HIV or hepatitis B drugs.
